findings.evidence: KostantForm.lean:174-179 proves the lemma from `ringChoose_mem_kostantForm` alone; `ringChooseSpan_le_iff` (Binomial.lean:118) is proved from `AddSubgroup.closure_le`, with no reference to `choose_mul_choose`.
findings.fix: Either drop the false connective ("Independently of that rule, the span of the coefficients in one designated Cartan vector lies in the form"), or add the statement that actually uses the product rule, e.g. `Subring.closure (Set.range (Ring.choose (ι ℚ (h i)))) ≤ kostantForm e h` combined with `mem_subringClosure_range_ringChoose`, so the advertised consequence is the one proved.
findings.issue: The doc says the Cartan--Cartan rule is `choose_mul_choose` and "Consequently `TauCeti.ringChooseSpan` for any designated Cartan vector lies in the Kostant form". That containment is not a consequence of the product rule: `ringChooseSpan_le_kostantForm` (line 176) is `ringChooseSpan_le_iff.2` applied to `ringChoose_mem_kostantForm`, i.e. plain closure monotonicity, and would hold verbatim if `choose_mul_choose` did not exist. The doc leads a reader to believe multiplicative closure of the Cartan part has been transferred to the Kostant form; it has not.

summary: The product formula, the span-is-a-subring results, and the subring/span identification are all mathematically correct and verified against Mathlib's `Ring.add_choose_eq` and `Ring.choose_smul_choose`, with no vacuity or hidden assumptions. Only defect: the KostantForm module doc asserts a logical dependency that does not exist.
